name: progressor-mcp

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Compact summary of every Goal this Session holds (current Task, open Detour, Tasks with a helper or waiting on the Developer, next Task, decisions and open notes) and the Developer's Standing Instructions. Call it at the start of every conversation and after context compression. With project, another project's Goals and Tasks instead, to change them from here. With for_helper, only the Developer's rules as a block to paste into the brief of a helper agent you start (helpers don't see the Standing Instructions, so include it whenever you brief one).

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

check.description: Also run the plan check-up and list everything it found.

for_helper.description: Only the rules, as a block for a helper agent's brief: the rules and context for everything, then this project's Standing Instructions, hard rules first.

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Look up one Goal, Task, Detour, decision, note or Standing Instruction by its ref (progressor://<goal>/<item>, or progressor://roadmap/<instruction>), with its file and line. Use it when the Developer pastes a ref or you need one item's details; for where the work stands overall, use get_status.

ref.description: A ref such as progressor://login/t2 or progressor://roadmap/i1.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: add_goal
tools.description: Add a Goal to the end of the Roadmap, with an optional Task list and Outcome; with claim: true, also claim it to start work. A title another Goal already has is refused unless allow_duplicate is set. To record work already finished, set done on the Goal and on every Task. Plan each Goal with an Outcome (one sentence on what done looks like) and Tasks that each have a short title, the files they touch, a one-line summary and an estimate. Tell the Developer the plan in a few plain lines first. With claim: true the answer is the whole status.

title.description: A few words naming the Goal, such as 'Ship OAuth login'.

id.description: A short ID for the Goal's refs, such as 'web-ui': lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Made from the title when left out.

outcome.description: What done looks like, in one sentence, such as 'Users can sign in with Google and stay signed in for 30 days'.

estimate.description: How long the whole Goal should take, such as '6h', when its Tasks are not estimated one by one yet. Without it, the Goal's estimate is the sum of its Tasks'.

title.description: A short title for the Task, a few words, such as 'Fix callback redirect loop'.

summary.description: One or two sentences on the fix or change the Task makes, such as 'Callback re-sets the session cookie on every hit; only set it after token exchange.'

code.description: Files the Task touches, optionally with :line.

estimate.description: How long it should take, such as '45m', '2h' or '1h 30m'. Give one for every Task you plan; the dashboard's schedule is built from them.

done.description: Add the Task already done, for work finished before it was recorded.

allow_duplicate.description: Add the Goal even though another Goal has the same title.

done.description: Record a Goal that is already finished. Every Task must then have done: true.

claim.description: Claim the new Goal straight away, to start working on it. Not with project: a Goal on another project's plan can't be claimed from here.

waits_on.description: Goals it waits on: IDs here, or <project>/<goal-id>.

release.description: Make it a release goal: it bundles the finished goals no earlier release took, and the reply gives the facts to write the changelog entry and version bump from.

bundles.description: For a release goal: the finished goals it bundles, by ID, instead of all the unreleased ones.

repeat.description: Make it come back: 1d, 1w, 2w, 1mo or a weekday (monday). A goal like it is added by itself when due, once the last one is finished or dropped.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: add_hotfix
tools.description: Add a hotfix: a bug the Developer wants fixed before any other work, often from a customer report. Pass the report word for word. It goes at the top of the Roadmap with two Tasks (a test that shows the bug, then the fix), and every Session is told it is waiting until one claims it. With claim: true, claim it now; otherwise finish the step you are on first, then claim it.

report.description: The bug report as the Developer or customer wrote it: what goes wrong, and how to make it happen if known.

title.description: A few words naming the bug; the report's first line when left out.

claim.description: Claim the hotfix straight away, to start on it now. Not with project: a hotfix on another project's plan can't be claimed from here.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Rename a Goal, set its Outcome or its estimate, or mark it needed for the launch (for_launch). Its ID, refs and Plan File stay the same, and it needs no Claim. To change a Goal's Tasks, claim it and use add_tasks, update_task or update_tasks.

goal.description: The Goal ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'.

outcome.description: The new Outcome; an empty string removes it.

estimate.description: How long the whole Goal should take, such as '6h'; it covers the open Tasks that have no estimate of their own. An empty string removes it, so the Goal's estimate is the sum of its Tasks'.

waits_on.description: The goals it waits on, replacing any it had (empty: none): IDs here, or <project>/<goal-id>.

for_launch.description: true: the Goal is needed for the launch, so the dashboard's Ready to launch? page and launch_readiness count it; false: no longer. Mark the goals a launch needs as soon as you know; nobody has to ask.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: launch_readiness
tools.description: Answer 'are we ready to launch?': what still stands before the launch or the next release, grouped by who it waits on (you, the Developer, other people), with serious risks nothing is reducing. It is the same summary as the dashboard's Ready to launch? page, so answer from it. It counts the next open release goal and what it bundles, else the goals marked for launch (update_goal for_launch), else every open goal.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: move_goal
tools.description: Move a Goal right before or after another Goal, so the Roadmap lists the work in the order it should happen. Give exactly one of before and after. The dashboard lists the Goals that need the Developer (things to try, steps to check, questions) in this order too, so put the one they should check first in front.

goal.description: The Goal ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'.

before.description: The ID of the Goal to move it in front of.

after.description: The ID of the Goal to move it behind.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: drop_goal
tools.description: Drop a Goal that will not be done, with the reason; its Plan File stays as a record. Releases this Session's Claim on it. A Goal another running Session holds, or one already done, cannot be dropped. To drop a single Task, use update_tasks (action drop).

goal.description: The Goal ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'.

reason.description: Why the Goal will not be done.

stop_repeating.description: For a goal a routine made: also stop the routine, so it won't come back.

tools.name: claim_goal
tools.description: Claim a Goal for this Session, so only this Session works on it. The Session keeps any other Goals it holds; while it holds several, pass goal to the tools that change one. Fails if another running Session holds it. Claiming a done Goal reopens it: its finished Tasks stay done, and add_tasks adds the new work to the same list.

goal.description: The Goal ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'.

takeover.description: Take the Goal from another running Session. Only when the Developer asks for it.

tools.name: resource
tools.description: A named shared resource that only one session or helper can use at a time (a dev window that allows a single instance, plasmashell, a port). claim it before you or a helper start something that needs it: refused, saying who holds it, since when and why, when someone else has it; then do not start it, do other work and try again later (nothing waits for you). Claiming your own again refreshes its time. It frees itself after `minutes` (30 unless given, at most 240) from the last claim, when its Session ends, or when you release it. A helper usually cannot call Progressor: claim on its behalf with label such as 'helper: media run'. release it as soon as the work that needed it ends (a helper's too), with the same label; another holder's is refused unless force, only when the Developer says the holder is gone. list says who holds what (get_status shows the same).

resource.description: The shared thing's name, such as 'dev-window' or 'plasmashell'. Case and spaces do not matter.

reason.description: To claim: why you need it, in a few words, such as 'running the UI test'. Shown to whoever is refused.

label.description: Who it is held for when that is not this Session itself, such as 'helper: media run'. Claim and release a helper's lock with the same label.

task.description: To claim: the Task ID it is for, such as 't3'.

minutes.description: To claim: how long to keep it before it frees itself, from now. 30 if omitted; claim again to extend.

force.description: To release: even though someone else holds it. Only when the Developer asks.

tools.name: release_goal
tools.description: Release this Session's Claim on a Goal, leaving it paused for a later Session.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

tools.name: complete_goal
tools.description: Mark the claimed Goal done and release it, once its Outcome is true and its Tasks are done, released or dropped (not with a helper, waiting on the Developer or only checked). While the Developer still has hand tests (save_hand_test) to mark, the Goal is released as built and waiting on their tests instead: it finishes by itself when they mark the last one, and a failure reopens it with a new Task. unmarked_hand_tests_ok finishes it now, only when the Developer says to finish anyway. If more work turns up later, claim_goal reopens it.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

unmarked_hand_tests_ok.description: Finish now even though some hand tests are still not marked by the Developer. Only when the Developer says to finish anyway.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: add_tasks
tools.description: Append Tasks to the claimed Goal's plan, each with an estimate of how long it takes. For work that is not part of the plan, declare a Detour instead. Set done on a Task that is already finished: a small change you have made is recorded in this one call, with hand_test for what the Developer should try. A quick fix that belongs to no Goal goes under Small fixes with add_small_fix instead.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

title.description: A short title for the Task, a few words, such as 'Fix callback redirect loop'.

summary.description: One or two sentences on the fix or change the Task makes, such as 'Callback re-sets the session cookie on every hit; only set it after token exchange.'

code.description: Files the Task touches, optionally with :line.

estimate.description: How long it should take, such as '45m', '2h' or '1h 30m'. Give one for every Task you plan; the dashboard's schedule is built from them.

done.description: Add the Task already done, for work finished before it was recorded.

hand_test.description: Something only the Developer can try by hand for this Task; added as a hand test about it, as with save_hand_test.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: add_small_fix
tools.description: Record a small one-off fix you have made that belongs to no Goal (a dev-server speed-up, a typo, formatting) as a finished step of the project's standing Small fixes goal, made the first time. Nothing is claimed and the Goals you hold are untouched. hand_test adds what the Developer should try. For work that is part of a Goal, use add_tasks with done: true instead.

title.description: A short title for the Task, a few words, such as 'Fix callback redirect loop'.

summary.description: One or two sentences on the fix or change the Task makes, such as 'Callback re-sets the session cookie on every hit; only set it after token exchange.'

code.description: Files the Task touches, optionally with :line.

hand_test.description: Something only the Developer can try by hand for this Task; added as a hand test about it, as with save_hand_test.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: save_risk
tools.description: Add a risk to the project's risks list: something that could go wrong, how likely and how bad, what would reduce it, who owns it and the goals that reduce it. Add the ones you notice as you work, without being asked; the Developer sees the list on the dashboard. With risk (its ID): change any of its fields, or its status (reduced once the work that lowers it is done, closed when it can no longer happen). Keep the list true as goals finish.

risk.description: A risk's ID, such as 'r2', to change it; leave out to add one (then title, likelihood and impact are needed).

title.description: What could go wrong, in a few words, such as 'Windows paths break setup'.

likelihood.description: How likely it is to happen: low, medium or high.

impact.description: How bad it would be: low, medium or high.

mitigation.description: What would reduce it, in one line; an empty string removes it.

owner.description: Who looks after it, such as 'your AI' or 'the Developer'; an empty string removes it.

goals.description: IDs of the goals whose work reduces it; replaces the ones it has.

status.description: open (the usual), reduced (the work that lowers it is done) or closed (it can no longer happen).

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: set_task_state
tools.description: Set a Task's state. 'with a helper': handed to a helper agent that is working on it (several Tasks can be). 'waiting on you': you are waiting on the Developer, such as for them to test something by hand; the dashboard shows the Goal as waiting on them, so tell them what you need. 'waiting on someone': waiting on a person other than the Developer (a team member, a lawyer, a provider): give person and need; it is shown apart from what waits on the Developer. 'checked': you checked a helper's work (tests, review) but it is not merged or released yet; give evidence, one short line on what you checked ("715 passed, live send OK"), which the Developer sees on the step. With 'with a helper', give helper_branch, helper_folder (the worktree path) and helper_label: they are recorded with the Task and shown in get_status and on the dashboard, and get_status warns when a finished Task's helper branch still has unmerged work. 'released': merged and out (shipped, installed or published); counts as done. 'pending', 'in progress' and 'done' work too (in progress allows one Task of a Goal at a time). Set a state as soon as it changes, such as 'checked' right after you check a helper's work, so the Developer's dashboard keeps moving. If the project has a helper limit (get_status shows it), keep at most that many Tasks with a helper: one more is still set, with a warning. To drop a Task, use update_tasks (action drop).

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

helper_branch.description: With state 'with a helper': the git branch the helper works on, such as 'feat/export'. Recorded so a branch left behind can be found later.

helper_folder.description: With state 'with a helper': the helper's worktree folder (its path).

helper_label.description: With state 'with a helper': a label for the helper, such as the model it runs on ('Sonnet').

evidence.description: With state 'checked': one short line on what you checked, such as '715 passed, live send OK'. Give it: the Developer sees it on the dashboard step.

person.description: With state 'waiting on someone': who it waits on, by name (or ID, such as 'p2'), such as 'Priya' or 'Stripe support'. Someone new is added to the project's people.

need.description: With state 'waiting on someone': what they need to do, in one line, such as 'Sign and send back the contract'.

role.description: With person: what they are to the project, such as 'payments lawyer'; kept on the project's people (an empty role removes it).

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: update_tasks
tools.description: Start, complete or drop Tasks, one or several in one call: start one before you change code for it (only one Task of a Goal is in progress at a time); complete it when done, with the files it touched (code), and the new summary when what you built differs from it; drop one that is no longer needed, with the reason. Also sets states and estimates. The operations are applied in order, so a start can follow the complete of the Task that was in progress; if any one fails, none is applied. A 'state' operation takes the same helper_branch, helper_folder, helper_label (with 'with a helper') and evidence (with 'checked') as set_task_state. Each operation can name its own claimed Goal with goal, else the call's goal (or the only Goal held) is used. Answers briefly, with the time a completed Task took and where the work stands, not the whole status.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

helper_branch.description: With state 'with a helper': the git branch the helper works on, such as 'feat/export'. Recorded so a branch left behind can be found later.

helper_folder.description: With state 'with a helper': the helper's worktree folder (its path).

helper_label.description: With state 'with a helper': a label for the helper, such as the model it runs on ('Sonnet').

evidence.description: With state 'checked': one short line on what you checked, such as '715 passed, live send OK'. Give it: the Developer sees it on the dashboard step.

person.description: With state 'waiting on someone': who it waits on, by name (or ID, such as 'p2'), such as 'Priya' or 'Stripe support'. Someone new is added to the project's people.

need.description: With state 'waiting on someone': what they need to do, in one line, such as 'Sign and send back the contract'.

action.description: start: mark in progress. complete: mark done. state: set the state given in state. drop: drop it, with reason. estimate: only set its estimate.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

state.description: For action 'state': the new state, as in set_task_state.

reason.description: For action 'drop': why the Task is no longer needed.

code.description: For action 'complete': files the Task touched, optionally with :line.

commits.description: Short hashes of its commits; found from git when left out.

tests.description: The test run behind it, in a few words ('715 passed').

summary.description: One or two sentences on the fix or change the Task makes, such as 'Callback re-sets the session cookie on every hit; only set it after token exchange.'

estimate.description: The Task's new estimate, such as '45m' or '2h' (any action; needed for 'estimate'); an empty string removes it.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: move_task
tools.description: Move a Task of a claimed Goal to another Goal when it belongs there. It keeps its title, summary, files and state, gets a new ID at the end of the other Goal's list (or right before or after the Task given in before or after) and a 'moved from' line. In the old Goal it stays as a dropped Task whose reason is where it went, so refs and history still work. The other Goal must not be dropped, done or held by another running Session; a Task in progress can move only if the other Goal has none in progress.

goal.description: The claimed Goal the Task is in. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

to_goal.description: The ID of the Goal to move the Task to.

before.description: A Task ID in the other Goal to put it in front of.

after.description: A Task ID in the other Goal to put it behind.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Change a Task's title, summary, files or estimate, for instance when the fix turns out different from the plan or you learn it takes longer. Leaves its status alone.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

title.description: A short title for the Task, a few words, such as 'Fix callback redirect loop'.

summary.description: One or two sentences on the fix or change the Task makes, such as 'Callback re-sets the session cookie on every hit; only set it after token exchange.'

code.description: The Task's files, optionally with :line; replaces the ones it has.

estimate.description: The Task's new estimate, such as '45m' or '2h'; an empty string removes it.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: start_detour
tools.description: Declare that the work is splitting off from the planned Tasks, before doing it. Branches from the current Task. Only one Detour can be open.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

title.description: What the Detour does, such as 'Fix flaky token refresh'.

reason.description: Why the work has to split off from the plan now.

tools.name: end_detour
tools.description: End the open Detour. 'merge back': it was small and is done; the plan is unchanged. 'return': go back to the plan, appending `tasks` for the Detour's intended work if any. 'recalibrate': drop every remaining Task and replace them with `tasks`.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

tasks.description: Tasks to append (return) or the new Task list (recalibrate).

title.description: A short title for the Task, a few words, such as 'Fix callback redirect loop'.

summary.description: One or two sentences on the fix or change the Task makes, such as 'Callback re-sets the session cookie on every hit; only set it after token exchange.'

code.description: Files the Task touches, optionally with :line.

estimate.description: How long it should take, such as '45m', '2h' or '1h 30m'. Give one for every Task you plan; the dashboard's schedule is built from them.

tools.name: save_decision
tools.description: Record a choice made for a claimed Goal along the way, such as 'old models get thinking on/off only', so it survives context compression; get_status shows it with its ID (c1, c2...). With id: reword it, or remove it with an empty text. Not for lasting project rules (save_standing_instruction) or project-wide background (update_context).

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

id.description: A decision's ID, such as 'c2', to change it; leave out to add one.

text.description: The decision, in one line; with id, empty removes it.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: save_note
tools.description: Note something you spotted that belongs to a Goal, such as a bug found during cleanup that belongs to the Voice Goal, instead of dealing with it now. Any Goal on the Roadmap that is not dropped, claimed or not. get_status shows the open notes of the Goals this Session holds. With id: resolve it once dealt with (resolved: true), reopen it (false), reword it, or remove it with an empty text.

goal.description: The ID of the Goal the note belongs to.

id.description: A note's ID, such as 'n2', to change it; leave out to add one.

text.description: What you spotted, in one line; with id, the new wording, and empty removes the note.

resolved.description: With id: true once the note is dealt with; false to reopen it.

project.description: Another project's plan to use instead of this one's: its name or ID on the dashboard, or its folder's full path. Changes there are marked as made from this project. Leave out for this project.

tools.name: ask_developer
tools.description: Ask the Developer a question on the dashboard, with 2 to 4 short choices they can click (they can also answer in their own words), instead of stopping in the chat. Use it for product and UX choices only they can make; carry on with other work meanwhile. Their answer reaches you at your next Progressor call, under 'New from the Developer', and is kept as a decision on the Goal. While a question is open the dashboard shows the Goal as waiting on them. To offer ways to go instead, give alternatives and recommended: nobody has to pick, you go ahead with yours. To take back a question that no longer needs an answer, pass withdraw with its ID instead.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

question.description: The question, in one plain sentence a non-programmer understands.

choices.description: 2 to 4 short answers to pick from, such as ['On by default', 'Follow the computer'].

alternatives.description: 2 to 4 ways to go, instead of choices: a title, a line about it, a picture ID from attach_picture.

recommended.description: The alternative you would pick (1-based; default 1).

wait.description: How long to wait for a pick before going ahead with yours, such as "10m"; default from the settings ("0m": at once).

task.description: The ID of the Task it is about, such as 't3'.

withdraw.description: The ID of an open question to withdraw (such as 'q2'), instead of asking a new one.

tools.name: reply_to_developer
tools.description: Answer a message the Developer sent you on the dashboard (shown under 'New from the Developer' with its ID, such as m2): say in a sentence or two, in plain words, what you did or will do about it. The reply shows under their message on the dashboard. Reply to every message, even if only to say you will do it later. A message to the whole project is answered with whole_project: true and needs no Goal.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

reply.description: Your answer, in plain words for someone who doesn't code.

whole_project.description: True for a message to the whole project rather than to a Goal.

tools.name: save_hand_test
tools.description: Add something only the Developer can try by hand to a claimed Goal, such as 'OpenCode may ask permission to read an attached file: allow it and check the reply'. Put it here instead of in your chat summary: the Developer sees the Goal's hand-test list on the dashboard and marks each one there as works, doesn't work (with a note) or won't test. A failure adds a Task to the Goal by itself; get_status shows what is still open and the new marks. complete_goal with tests unmarked leaves the Goal waiting on them, and it finishes when the last is marked. With id: reword it, change which Task it is about, or remove it with an empty text (for one that turned out not to need testing); its mark stays, and only the Developer marks tests.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

id.description: A hand test's ID, such as 'h2', to change it; leave out to add one.

text.description: What to try and what to look for, in one or two short plain sentences; with id, empty removes it.

task.description: The ID of the Task it is about, such as 't3'; with id, an empty string removes the link.

tools.name: attach_picture
tools.description: Show the Developer a screenshot or a short screen recording on the dashboard instead of naming a file in chat. It is copied (not moved) next to the plan, stays on this computer and out of git, and appears on the Goal, on the step or on the hand test you name; the Developer clicks it to enlarge. Allowed: .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif and .webm .mp4, up to 10 MB, with a short caption. To take one back, pass remove with its ID (such as 'p2') instead.

goal.description: The claimed Goal's ID, such as 'ship-oauth-login'. Needed only when this Session holds several Goals.

path.description: The file's path, absolute or from the project's folder.

caption.description: What it shows, in a few plain words (up to 200 characters).

task.description: The ID of the Task it is about, such as 't3'.

hand_test.description: The ID of the hand test it is about, such as 'h2'.

remove.description: The ID of a picture to remove (such as 'p2'), instead of attaching one.

tools.name: save_standing_instruction
tools.description: Save a lasting rule from the Developer about how you should work in this project, such as 'ask me before changing the plan'. get_status lists it from then on. Use it only for rules meant to last; a one-off request is just done. A rule the Developer says holds in every project ('in all my projects...', 'always, everywhere...') goes in with global: true: it is saved once for this computer and every project's get_status shows it. With id (s1, s2... in get_status; g1, g2... for a rule for everything): reword it when the Developer changes it, make it hard (hard: true) or ordinary again (false), set the helper limit it holds, or remove it with an empty text. What you leave out stays.

id.description: A rule's ID, such as 's2', or 'g1' for a rule for everything, to change it; leave out to add one.

text.description: The rule, in the Developer's words where possible; with id, empty removes it and left out keeps the wording.

hard.description: true for a rule that must never be broken (not just a preference); get_status and the session start list those first as HARD RULE.

helpers_at_once.description: Makes this rule the project's helper limit: the most Tasks that may be 'with a helper' at once, such as 2 when the Developer says 'at most 2 helpers in parallel'. One rule holds the limit; setting it here takes it off any other. 0 removes it.

global.description: true for a rule for everything: the Developer says it holds in all their projects ('in all my projects...'). Saved once for this computer; shown wherever Progressor runs.

tools.name: update_context
tools.description: Replace the project's Important context: lasting background you and the Developer need in every conversation, such as what the project is, key facts, where things live and choices that hold for the whole project. Not for rules (save_standing_instruction) or for one Goal's details. get_status shows the current text: send the whole new text, or an empty text to clear it. At most 4000 characters.

text.description: The whole Important context, in plain words; short paragraphs or a list.

global.description: true to replace a part of the context for everything instead (every project, and anywhere Progressor runs on this computer). Only when the Developer asks for it. Give part too.

part.description: With global: "computer" for About this computer (setup facts: the operating system, tools, where CI runs, hardware), "me" for About me and how I work (the Developer's preferences).

tools.name: plan_history
tools.description: The plan's recent changes (who, when, what). restore: <id> goes back to before that change; that can be undone too.

restore.description: A change's ID from the list.

list.description: How many changes to list; 10 unless set.

tools.name: handoff
tools.description: A markdown handoff of a stretch of work, for whoever picks it up next. Without text: the facts for the range (steps, decisions, open items, commits, files). Write the handoff from them, then call again with text and title to save it for the dashboard.

since.description: A date (2026-11-01) or a commit to start after; the last handoff when left out.

until.description: A date to end at; now when left out.

commits.description: Exactly these commits, instead of a range.

text.description: The handoff you wrote, in markdown.

instructions:
Progressor keeps the plan for this project in .progressor/ and shows it to the Developer on a live dashboard. Change the plan only with these tools, never by editing those files. The Developer may not be a programmer: you run the plan, they watch.

1. At the start of every conversation and after context compression, call get_status and follow the Standing Instructions it lists. If it says one Goal is paused, claim it (claim_goal) and carry on.
2. When the Developer asks for work no Goal covers, plan it as a Goal: a short title, an Outcome (one sentence) and Tasks, each with the files it touches, a one-line summary and an estimate ("45m", "2h"). Tell the Developer the plan in a few plain lines, then add_goal with claim: true. A quick question needs no Goal.
3. Before code for a Task longer than a few minutes, start it with update_tasks; when done, complete it there with the files touched, and the new summary if the work differs; drop what is not needed. Record a small finished change in one call: add_tasks with done: true (and hand_test if the Developer should try it). Keep summaries and estimates true with update_task. set_task_state records Tasks in other hands (with a helper, waiting on you, checked, released); keep to any helper limit get_status shows.
4. To change several Tasks at once, give update_tasks several operations (applied in order, all or nothing). move_task moves a Task to another Goal. To hold several Goals, claim each one and pass goal (its ID) to the tools that change a Goal.
5. About to change code for something that is not the current Task? Call start_detour with the reason first; afterwards end_detour ("merge back", "return" or "recalibrate").
6. When every Task is done, released or dropped and the Outcome is true, call complete_goal and tell the Developer in one sentence.
7. Talk to the Developer in everyday words: say "step" for Task and "side trip" for Detour, and leave out tool names, IDs and the files in .progressor/. Give them the dashboard link from get_status at the start and when a Goal is finished.
8. A lasting rule ("always...", "never...") is saved with save_standing_instruction (with its id, changes or removes one); one that must never be broken ("never", "hard rule") with hard: true; one for all their projects ("in all my projects") with global: true. update_context keeps the project's Important context page; save_decision records a choice that is not a project rule; save_note records something that belongs to a Goal instead of fixing it now.
9. Anything only the Developer can try by hand goes in save_hand_test, not in your chat summary. Show a screenshot or recording with attach_picture instead of naming a file.
10. The Developer can write to you on the dashboard: their messages and answers arrive at the end of your next Progressor reply under "New from the Developer". Act on each one and answer with reply_to_developer (whole_project: true to message the whole project). For a product or UX choice, use ask_developer with 2 to 4 short choices instead of stopping in the chat.
11. When you brief a helper agent, paste in get_status with for_helper: true; helpers don't see the Standing Instructions. Before starting something only one can use at a time (a dev window, a port), claim it with resource; release it there when done.
12. Work that belongs to another project using Progressor goes in that project's plan: pass project (its name on the dashboard) to get_status, add_goal and the other tools that take it.
13. A * line in .progressor/.gitignore keeps the plan out of git; delete it to keep it in git.
